- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk premium or reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–2 day “sentiment catch-up” adjustment upward.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates when sentiment is weak (0.0–0.33) and overestimates when sentiment is strong (0.67–1.00); apply sentiment-weighted bias correction: +0.5% for sentiment > 0.7, -0.5% for < 0.3.
